documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
WELCOME TO MEDICARE VISIT
65F, now on Medicare. Fully vaccinated for COVID.
Health risk assessment reviewed: lives alone in a single-floor home, independent in ADLs/IADLs, drives, no falls in the past year, no hearing complaints. Uses glasses.
Smoking: 1 ppd, 35 pack-years. Quitting "someday."
Depression screen negative. Cognition: no concerns from her, conversational and organized; no formal testing indicated.
Advance directive: daughter is her health care proxy; form on file? -- she'll bring a copy.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
Exam: BMI 33. Normal exam. Vision screen with glasses grossly ok on wall chart.
Plan:
- DXA (age 65) and annual LDCT ordered.
- Mammogram 11/2020 neg. Colonoscopy due 2026.
- Pneumococcal vaccine: discussed, she wants to space it from the COVID shots; next visit.
- Labs drawn. Follow up in 6 weeks for DM visit -- she mentioned her glasses "don't seem right lately," will look at that then.

documents.title: Office Visit: Vision change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since around Christmas her vision in both eyes has been getting gradually worse -- reading signs while driving at dusk, bumping the doorframe on the left a couple of times. No pain, no red eyes, no discharge, no flashes or floaters, no headaches. Hasn't seen the optometrist since 2019.
DM otherwise fine.
O: Vitals as charted. VA with her glasses 20/40 both eyes on the wall chart. Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. Conjunctivae clear. Undilated fundi limited. Confrontation fields: possibly reduced peripherally on both sides, hard to be sure.
A1c drawn.
A/P:
1. Gradual painless bilateral vision loss -- needs a full dilated exam with pressures and fields. Ophthalmology referral placed (not just optometry). Family hx glaucoma in maternal grandmother noted on referral.
2. T2DM - A1c today. Continue metformin.
Advised not to drive at night until seen.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY CONSULTATION -- date of service 06/10/2021
Referred by primary care for vision loss.

History: Over roughly six months both eyes have slowly lost clarity. Painless. She has had no redness or discharge. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Smoker, 35 pack-years. Maternal grandmother had glaucoma.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Examination:
Visual acuity reduced in each eye.
Intraocular pressure (Goldmann): 28 mmHg OD, 27 mmHg OS.
Gonioscopy: angles open 360 degrees both eyes. Anterior chambers deep and quiet.
Optic nerves: enlarged cup-to-disc ratio both eyes.
Humphrey visual fields: central fields preserved; peripheral field loss in both eyes.
Dilated fundus: no diabetic retinopathy; macula flat.

Impression: Primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes.
Plan: Start latanoprost 0.005%, one drop in each eye at bedtime. Reviewed drop technique and the possibility of iris darkening and lash growth. Recheck pressure in 8 weeks. Fields and OCT yearly. Okay to drive in daylight.
Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Pharmacy question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy called: new latanoprost Rx from ophthalmology, wanted to confirm no drug interactions with her list before filling. None. Generic covered, no PA needed. Added to med list from consult letter.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Glaucoma follow-up, seen 08/10/2021. Using latanoprost nightly, no irritation. IOP 18 OD, 17 OS -- good response. Nerves unchanged. Continue latanoprost. Return in one year with fields and OCT, sooner for any change in vision.

documents.title: Office Visit: Hand pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Both hands have hurt more and more over the past year. Worst first thing in the morning, loosens up as she gets going. Hard to open jars. No redness or heat in the joints, no rashes, no fevers. Got her booster at the pharmacy 10/12.
O: knobby DIP and PIP joints both hands, mildly tender. No synovitis that I can feel. Wrists normal. Grip slightly reduced from pain.
A/P: Likely osteoarthritis of the hands, but morning-predominant pain -- she'd like a specialist opinion and so would I. Rheumatology referral. Acetaminophen OK meanwhile, up to 3 g/day. Avoid regular ibuprofen with her BP if she can.

medications.sig: Take 1-2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for joint pain (max 3,000 mg/day)

reports.text: Bilateral hands, three views each. Joint space loss at the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints with subchondral sclerosis and marginal osteophytes. No erosions. Bone mineralization normal. No fracture.
reports.conclusion: Osteoarthritis of the interphalangeal joints of both hands.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY NEW CONSULT -- visit 11/29/2021
Reason: hand pain, referred by PCP.

Ms. Klein, 65, reports a year of progressively worse pain in both hands. It is at its worst on waking and eases as she uses her hands during the day. No joint redness or warmth. Background: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed open-angle glaucoma.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, latanoprost drops. NKDA.
Social: current smoker, 35 pack-years; no alcohol; retired retail supervisor.
Family: sister with osteoarthritis.

Exam: Bony hypertrophy of the DIP and PIP joints bilaterally with mild tenderness to palpation. Crepitus on passive range of motion. No erythema, warmth or soft-tissue swelling. MCPs and wrists spared.
Hand radiographs (today): joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and periarticular osteophytes at the involved joints, no erosive change.

Assessment: Primary osteoarthritis of the hands. No features of an inflammatory arthritis.
Plan: Acetaminophen scheduled or as needed; hand therapy exercises (handout given); paraffin/warm soaks in the morning. Return as needed or if other joints become involved.

documents.title: Rheumatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did you get the letter from the arthritis doctor? She said it's just wear and tear, take Tylenol. Is that it? I thought maybe there was a pill.

documents.title: RE: Rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got it, thanks. I agree with her -- osteoarthritis in the finger joints, not the inflammatory kind. Acetaminophen plus the hand exercises and warm water in the mornings is the right start. Anti-inflammatories carry more risk for your kidneys and blood pressure, so I'd hold off. We'll keep an eye on it.
